S1:11.text: And when he was come to a certaine place, and would reſt in it after ſunne ſet, he tooke one of the ſtones that lay there, and putting it vnder his head, ſlept in the ſame place.

S1:14.text: And thy ſeed ſhal be as the duſt of the earth thou ſhalt be dilated to the Weſt, and to the Eaſt, &C to the North, and to the South and in thee and thy ſeed al the tribes of the earth SHAL BE BLESSED.

S1:19.text: And he called the name of the citie Bethel, which before was called Luza.

S1:2.text: but goe, and make a iourney into Meſopotamia of Syria, to the houſe of Bathuel thy mothers father, and take thee a wife thence of the daughters of Laban thin vntle.

S1:21.text: and I ſhal be returned proſperouſly to my fathers houſe, the Lord ſhal be my God,

S1:7.text: and that Iacob obeying his parents was gone into Syria:

S1:9.text: he went to Iſmael, and tooke to wife beſides them, which he had before, Maheleth the daughter of Iſmael Abrahams ſonne, ſiſter to Nabaioth. Thertore

S3:12.text: And he ſaw in his ſleepe a ladder ſtanding vpon the earth, and the top therof tooching heauen the angels alſo of God aſcending and deſcending by it,

S3:13.text: and our Lord leyning vpon the ladder ſaying to him I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Iſaac: the Land, wherin thou ſleepeſt, I wil geue to thee and to thy ſeed.

S3:14.text: And thy ſeed ſhal be as the duſt of the earth thou ſhalt be dilated to the Weſt, and to the Eaſt, &C to the North, and to the South: and IN THEE and thy ſeed al the tribes of the earth SHAL BE BLESSED.

S3:17.text: And trembling he ſaid How terrible is this place this is none other but the houſe of God, and the gate of heauen.

S3:21.text: and I ſhal be returned proſperouſly to my fathers houſe, the Lord ſhal be my God,

S3:3.text: And God almightie bleſſe thee, and make thee encreaſe encreaſe, and multiplie thee that thou maieſt be into multitudes of peoples.

S3:6.text: And Eſau ſeing that his father had bleſſed Iacob, and had ſent him into Meſopotamia of Syria, to marry a wife thence; and that after the bleſſing he had commanded him, ſaying: Thou ſhalt not take a wife of the daughters of Chanaan:

S3:7.text: and that Iacob obeying his parents was gone into Syria:

S3:8.text: hauing tryal alſo that his father did not willingly ſee the daughters of Canaan:

S3:9.text: he went to Iſmael, and tooke to wife beſides them, which he had before, Maheleth the daughter of Iſmael Abrahams ſonne, ſiſter to Nabaioth. Therfore

S6:15.text: And I wil be thy keeper whither ſo-euer thou goeſt, and wil bring thee back into this land: neither wil I leaue thee, til I ſhal haue accompliſhed al things which I haue ſaid.

S6:3.text: And God Almightie bleſſe thee, and make thee encreaſe, and multiplie thee: that thou mayeſt be into multitudes of peoples.

S6:4.text: And giue he thee the bleſſings of Abraham, and to thy ſeed after thee: that thou mayeſt poſſeſſe the land of thy peregrination, which he promiſed to thy grandfather.
